title: ExtractRequest
description: A request to extract documents into a load Ingest created.

adjudication.description: Optional model-selected linking. `adjudication.auto` defaults to false.

asked_apart.description:
Links asked apart from the others, in calls of their own: the links a load moved to
this version gained ([`Fold`]). Every other call is made as if the ontology lacked them,
so it replays what the documents' saved work holds. Each must be declared. Which a
document is asked is what its saved work for its text holds (`artifacts`): a document
asked before a move is asked none of them, so a rebuild of a moved load costs nothing
and holds what it held; a document with no saved work for its text is asked all of them,
in one pass of its own chunked as every link pass is, with its own verification. A
reply no link covered that a stated fact of one of them covers (the same section, quotes
that overlap) is not reviewed.

certified_acceptance.description:
Whether a fact is accepted, or held, by people's labels of its cell (its link, evidence
shape and score tenth) rather than by the verifier's score alone: `"off"`, the default,
or `{"on": certificate}`. A certificate judges only the claims of its `ontology_version`
scored by its `verifier` under its `prompt_version`, all three the run's; any other is
logged and judges nothing. One whose version is the request's and that names a link
`ontology_toml` lacks refuses the request. The document transactions of a run that
judges under one record the certificate's id, and the artifact key names it.

database.description: The graph written to; one request at a time writes to it.

decisions.description:
Settled review decisions snapshotted for this load: at most 10,000 of each kind, never
truncated. Two of one identity, a resolve decision without a document or a normalized
name, an alias without a normalized name or an entity, or a decision giving one of
`decision_id` and `decided_at` without the other, refuse the request; one that no longer
fits `ontology_toml` is counted (`totals.stale_decisions`) and left out, except a resolve
decision of a type it has, whose name is reviewed again rather than matched another way.
A value a property decision overwrites keeps the decision's `decision_id` and
`decided_at`, so the load tells when it was decided. A resolve decision sent with a
document the load holds writes what the name held back, where the load still asks about
it. An alias acts only on a document whose text writes its name: send those whose names
the request's documents write, which leaves the run as every alias the load carries
would.

documents.description:
The documents, extracted up to `limits.documents_in_flight` at once and committed one
at a time.

dry_run.description: Read the store but write nothing.

fold.description:
Moves the load in place from the version it was written with to `ontology_version`,
before anything else, if the change only adds what none of its documents was asked
([`heal::fold::classify`]): links that are neither required nor derive anything nor are
stated by rows, routes gaining exactly them, and descriptions no route reads. Its
`fold` event says what came of it. It takes no documents, no `remove` and no decisions, and
does nothing else: the version's labels recorded, the run ends `done`. The load's
marker must record `fold.from_version`, which it then records `ontology_version` in place
of (`moved`), or `ontology_version` already, as after a run that moved it (`moved`
again, writing nothing); any other is `marker_elsewhere`, and the run ends
`load_mismatch`. One that adds anything else writes nothing (`not_additive`, with why),
and the run ends `done` with nothing done. Absent, a load stays at the version it was
written with.

load.description:
The load written to, the backend's current one. Ingest must have created it with
`ontology_version`, and it must not be being deleted; otherwise nothing is written
(`load_unknown`, `load_mismatch`).

mappings_toml.description:
The approved `mappings.toml`. Its `[extractions]` routes give each document set's
scope: what its documents may name, create, fill and link. A document of a set no route
reads is stored with its sections, unread (`out_of_scope`).

models.description:
The models that extract and verify. The endpoint's API key travels in the call's
metadata, never here.

ontology_version.description: The version the graph records, in place of the one `ontology_toml` declares.

remove.description:
Documents to take out of the load before the request's are extracted, by id: each one's
sections, mentions, quotes and reviews, each fact's confidence recomputed from what is
left, and the facts and entities left with nothing are deleted (`document_removed`). A
document the load doesn't hold is skipped, so a retry removes nothing twice. Ignored on
a dry run.

request_id.description: The idempotency key: a retry sends the same one.

Adjudication.description:
Optional `ExtractRequest.adjudication`; `auto` is off unless explicitly enabled.
Suggestions are still recorded when it is off.

AwsRegion.description:
An AWS region, such as `us-east-1` or `ap-southeast-2`: its endpoint's host is built from
it, never typed.

AzureEndpoint.description:
An Azure OpenAI resource's endpoint: https on a host of `openai.azure.com`,
`cognitiveservices.azure.com` or `services.ai.azure.com`, with no port, user, query or
fragment, and no path but `/openai/v1`. It is kept as `{origin}/openai/v1`.

Bucket.description:
A tenth of verifier scores, from the review cut (0.6) up: the bands a review queue draws its
random slice from. Below the review cut a claim is refuted, never held, so no bucket.

oneOf.description: From 0.6 to under 0.7.
From 0.7 to under 0.8.
From 0.8 to under 0.9.
From 0.9: what the bar accepts.

Certificate.description:
The labels of facts of one ontology version, judged by one verifier model under one prompt
version, by cell. No cell is in it twice, no cell's counts overflow, and its id is the hash
of what it holds.

cells.description: Each cell's labels; a cell is listed once.

ontology_version.description:
The ontology version the labelled claims were judged under: the request's
`ontology_version`, or it judges nothing.

prompt_version.description: The engine's prompt version they were scored under: the engine's, or it judges nothing.

verifier.description:
The verifier model that scored them, by its id (provider, model and effort, such as
`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5@high`): the request's verifier, or it judges nothing.

CertifiedAcceptance.description: Whether facts are accepted by certificate: a request's switch, off by default.

oneOf.description: Every claim is judged under the fixed cuts.

The facts of the cells this certificate decides are judged by their labels, under the
version, verifier and prompts it was made for: a certified cell's accepted under the bar,
a breached cell's held at the bar too. Claims already held are not released by it.

CompatApi.description: The OpenAI API an OpenAI-compatible server speaks.

oneOf.description: `{base_url}/chat/completions`.
`{base_url}/responses`.

Decision.description:
One settled review: a link choice or a property value, never a mix of the two.
`entity_key` is the stored key encoding for keyed types, the normalized name for named ones.
Either may name the decision, by the backend's `decision_id` and when it was settled
(`decided_at`): both or neither, as one alone is refused. The version of a value a property
decision overwrites keeps them, so a load built since still tells when it was decided.

decided_at.description: When it was settled; given with `decision_id`.

decision_id.description: The decision's id, as the backend keeps it; given with `decided_at`.

decided_at.description: When it was settled; given with `decision_id`.

decision_id.description: The decision's id, as the backend keeps it; given with `decided_at`.

claim_key.description:
The claim's key, as the review stores it. A key the load holds no review under is
matched to the review at the quote's place that states what `statement_hash` binds.

decided_at.description:
When it was settled. Of a link that holds one value the approval also decides the
link, from the date its quote gives, else its document's date, else from this:
it beats undated statements and those dated up to then, and a statement dated later
beats it. Of two approvals of one link the later settled is the link's decision,
and the other's quote still states the link from its own date.

decision_id.description:
The decision's id, as the backend keeps it: one id is one decision. Of two
approvals of one link that holds one value settled at the same instant, the one
whose id sorts last is the link's decision.

doc_id.description: The document whose review holds the claim.

end.description: Where the review's quote ends in its section, after `start`.

section.description: The section of the review's quote, as the review stores it.

start.description: Where the review's quote starts in its section, as the review stores it.

statement_hash.description:
The hash of what the review stated when the person read it: its `suggested_link`, a
unit separator and its `statement`, as stored.

oneOf.description:
A withdrawal of a release decision: the release, as it was sent, whose approval the
person took back.

claim_key.description: The claim's key, as the release named it.

decided_at.description: When the release was settled, as it was sent.

decision_id.description: The release decision's id: what its release wrote is known by it.

doc_id.description: The document of the release it withdraws.

end.description: Where the review's quote ends in its section, as the release named it.

section.description: The section of the review's quote, as the release named it.

start.description: Where the review's quote starts in its section, as the release named it.

statement_hash.description: The hash of what the person read, as the release named it.

oneOf.description:
A name of a type a person linked to an entity, carried to every document of the load:
where a document's entity of the type has this as its fullest name and the names rung
finds no other entity for it, the name links the chosen entity, as a name the person
gave it. It acts only on a document whose text writes the name: its words, in order,
with nothing but what is no word between them, folded as names are matched. A
document's own resolve decision of the name wins. Two aliases of one name that choose
different entities carry neither. Send those whose names the request's documents write
(sending more changes nothing) to link the name in the documents the request lists,
those the load holds included.

decision_id.description: The decision's id, as the backend keeps it.

entity_key.description:
The entity chosen, as a resolve decision names it. Never null: "not in data" is one
document's to say.

norm_name.description: The name, normalized as a resolve decision's is.

Endpoint.description: The endpoint every model of a request is called on.

call_timeout_secs.description:
One JSON or text call's attempt, from connecting to its last byte, in seconds. Turns
are bounded by the request's wall time and an idle watchdog instead; an Ask turn, but
on Ollama, is also cut when no real output (keep-alives aside) arrives for a third of
the wall time, and tried once more.

max_calls_in_flight.description:
Calls in flight on this endpoint at once, across every request, model and kind of call;
none for no endpoint-wide bound. A local server takes one or a few.

provider.description: Who serves the models, and where.

artifacts.description:
Artifacts of earlier runs, under the files root. Every model call one of them holds
replays, with no cost; only the others are asked, such as the section calls a route's
new property changes.

doc_id.description: The backend's document id, which the graph records it by.

path.description: The text to read, under the files root.

set.description: The document set it belongs to, whose routes give its scope.

uri.description: Where the original is kept, recorded as the document's provenance; never read.

max_text_bytes.description: The largest document text read; a longer one fails `too_large`.

max_usd.description: Spend, in US dollars, checked before every model call.

ExtractModels.description: The models a document's extraction runs on.

verify.description: Judges whether the text states each fact.

Fold.description: The version a load is moved from in place ([`ExtractRequest::fold`]).

from_version.description: The version the load's marker records now.

HelixTarget.description: Where the graph is written: the backend's proxy for one Helix database.

max_request_bytes.description: The largest request body the proxy takes; a write past it is refused before it is sent.

timeout_secs.description: How long one request may take, in seconds.

token.description: The job's bearer token for the proxy.

LoadId.description: One load of an approved version into a graph: the id of the backend job that creates it, such as a ULID. One or more printable ASCII characters, no space.

MediaType.description:
Document formats that take the LLM path. Tables and code take deterministic routes and are
not documents.

oneOf.description: Markdown: sections break at headings too.
Plain text.

ModelName.description:
A model's name as its provider takes it: 1 to 200 characters, none of them whitespace or a
control character.

ModelSpec.description: What a request runs a role on.

context_tokens.description:
The context window: Ollama's `num_ctx`, elsewhere a bound the prompt is checked
against.

max_output_tokens.description: The most output one response may write, under the task's own ceiling.

name.description:
The model, as the provider names it (an Azure deployment's name, a Bedrock model or
inference profile id).

reasoning.description: Send the provider's reasoning knob (Anthropic's effort, OpenAI's reasoning effort).

revision.description: The Ollama model's digest the request was tested on.

ModelUrl.description:
The base URL of a server the request names: http or https, with a host, and with no user,
password, query or fragment; a path is kept, without a trailing `/`. Whether plain http or
a private address may be called is the server's to say ([`TurnModels::check`]).

OllamaDigest.description: An Ollama model's digest: `sha256:` and 64 lowercase hex digits.

oneOf.description: The model's row in Helix's price table.

Another model's row of the same provider kind: the model an Azure deployment runs, or
the model behind a Bedrock inference profile.
These rates.
Nothing: a local or self-hosted model.

Provider.description:
Who serves a request's models, and where. Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and Bedrock need
an API key; an Ollama server takes none; an OpenAI-compatible server may.

oneOf.description: Anthropic's API, `https://api.anthropic.com`.
OpenAI's API, `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
An Azure OpenAI resource; each model is a deployment's name.
Amazon Bedrock's runtime in a region, with a Bedrock API key.
An Ollama server.
A server speaking an OpenAI API.

base_url.description: Its base URL, the version path included, such as `https://llm.example.com/v1`.

Rates.description: Per-token rates, in nano-dollars ($1 per million tokens is 1,000).

cache_read.description: Input read from the provider's prompt cache; the input rate when none.

cache_write.description: Input written to the provider's prompt cache; the input rate when none.

SetId.description: The id of a document set, such as `set_01JDX4K2`: 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`.

Shape.description: How the document carries a claim ([`Shape::of`]).

oneOf.description: Plain text whose quote's passage (its sentence and one either side) names every end.
A list item: a bulleted or numbered line, or a value of a comma list under a label.
A row or cell of a table.
A heading, the document's title, or a labelled field ("Status: open").
Plain text whose section names every end, one of them outside the quote's passage.

Plain text with an end its section doesn't name: the document names it elsewhere, as
in a header or a heading above.
Plain text with an end the document names nowhere.

Tally.description:
Labelled claims, and how many of them were wrong: never more than there are. A label that
can't tell isn't counted.

errors.description: Of them, those labelled wrong: at most `n`.

n.description: Labelled claims, those that can't tell left out.

Value.description: A scalar property decision. Objects and arrays are refused at the contract boundary.

WireCell.description: A cell and its labels, as the contract writes them.

learn.description: The labels of claims of documents in the learn half, which picks the cells to test.

test.description: The labels of claims of documents in the held-out half, which tests them.
